# Fairstay Licensing Calendar (`fairstay-licensing-calendar`)

Licensing and credentialing calendar for nursing homes: facility licenses, Medicare and Medicaid revalidations, CLIA and other certificates, administrator and nurse licenses. Flags expired and expiring items, renewals pending past expiry, licensed staff with no license on file, and standard items missing for a facility. Staff names and license numbers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Licensing Calendar never files a renewal or revalidation with a state or CMS.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Change of ownership and licensing · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-licensing-calendar demo
npx -y fairstay-licensing-calendar mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional licenses for Cedar Hollow and Bluebonnet Manor, checked on 1 April 2026 with a 60-day warning. Planted:

- An RN license expired 15 March with no renewal on file.
- A CNA on the roster (written "C.N.A.") has no certification on the list.
- The Cedar Hollow CLIA certificate expired 20 March; the renewal was filed 25 February and is not yet issued.
- Bluebonnet Manor has no CLIA entry.
- An LPN license expires 30 April and the Medicare revalidation is due 15 May.
- The fire marshal inspection has no date.
- A dietary aide is on the roster and is correctly not checked for a license.

Staff names and license numbers are in [`phi-canaries.json`](fixtures/phi-canaries.json); they must never reach the model. [`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells `warn_days`, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `licensing_check` | Check every license, certificate and revalidation date, licensed staff against the list, and each facility against the standard items. | runs |
| `licensing_write_report` | Write licensing.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and licensing.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/licensing). | runs |
| `licensing_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `licensing_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `licensing_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `licensing_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `license_renewal_submit` | Fairstay Licensing Calendar never files a renewal or revalidation with a state or CMS. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `licensing_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `items` (required) | Licenses and certificates under --root: item, facility, holder, role, number, expiration date, renewal filed date |
| `staff` | Optional staff roster: name, role, facility (licensed roles must have a license on the list) |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: warn_days, facilities, licensed_roles |
| `as_of` | Status date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-licensing-calendar inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Licenses and certificates (`items`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `item` (required) | text | Item, License, Certificate, Credential, Type |
| `facility` | text | Facility, Building, Location |
| `holder` | text (masked) | Holder, Employee, Name, Licensee |
| `role` | text | Role, Position, Title, Discipline |
| `number` | text (masked) | Number, License Number, License #, Certificate Number, PTAN |
| `expires` | date | Expires, Expiration, Expiration Date, Exp Date, Due, Revalidation Due |
| `renewal_filed` | date | Renewal Filed, Renewal Submitted, Filed |

### Staff roster (`staff`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | text (masked) | Employee, Employee Name, Name, Staff |
| `role` (required) | text | Role, Position, Job Title, Title |
| `facility` | text | Facility, Building, Location |

## Settings file (`licensing_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `warn_days` | Flag items expiring within this many days (default 60) |
| `facilities` | Facility names to check for the standard items |
| `licensed_roles` | Roles that need a license on the list (default RN, LPN, LVN, CNA, Administrator, NHA, PT, OT, SLP, RD) |

## Memory

`licensing_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `licensing_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `licensing_note` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-licensing-calendar": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-licensing-calendar",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-licensing-calendar -- npx -y fairstay-licensing-calendar mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-licensing-calendar tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-licensing-calendar sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-licensing-calendar inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-licensing-calendar call licensing_check '{"items":"<items>"}'
fairstay-licensing-calendar eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-licensing-calendar demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
